title: What angle lies between the lines of an eight-petalled flower?
description: Eight equal petals meet at a centre along eight equally spaced lines. A full turn shared among eight equal angles gives the angle between neighbours, and it is built by bisecting a right angle. Keeko's doubt, that each angle is sixty degrees, is broken by counting how many fit round a point.
teaching_notes: One idea: equal angles round a point share a full turn, and half of a right angle is built by bisecting it. Watch for students who use sixty degrees because six triangles fit round a point.

source: Eight equal petals meet at a centre, along eight equally spa
video_script.why: The child can bisect an angle and build a right angle but has not yet used both to build an angle that is an eighth of a full turn.
video_script.substitution: A full turn shared among eight equal angles gives the angle, and bisecting a right angle builds it.
video_script.anchor: Eight equal petals meet at a centre along eight equally spaced lines: find the angle between neighbouring lines, and construct it.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko writes sixty degrees in every gap, because six triangles fit round a point. Eight angles of sixty degrees would overlap past a full turn.
video_script.payoff_line: Each angle is forty five degrees

final_answer.value: Each angle is 45°; construct 90° and bisect it
final_answer.spoken: each angle is forty five degrees, and we build it by making a ninety degree angle and bisecting it

never_show: the bisected right angle before the last steps
maths_rules: Eight equal angles round the centre make a full turn of 360 degrees.
360 / 8 = 45, so each angle is 45 degrees. Check: 8 x 45 = 360.
Construct a 90 degree angle at O with equal arcs, then bisect it: arcs from O cut the two arms at A and B, equal arcs from A and B meet at C, and OC makes 45 degrees with each arm by SSS.
Bisect one more right angle, and extend the lines through O, to get four lines: eight half-lines from O at 45 degrees to each other.
Slip: 60 degrees fits 6 times round a point, and 8 x 60 = 480, which is past a full turn.
video_script.design: One idea: share the full turn, then build half of a right angle. Keeko's doubt is sixty degrees, from six triangles round a point.
